component-o.description-s: 300 mA ultra-low-noise, low-IQ LDO, fixed 2.8 V output, active output discharge, SOT-23-5

non-technical-o.lifecycle-source-s: DigiKey: Active; TI package addendum: Active

cfgpins-ao.3c: EN active high (VEN(HI) 0.9 V max, VEN(LOW) 0.3 V min, p7); internal 500 k smart pulldown holds the LDO off when EN floats (p4): tied to IN, always on; a sequenced design drives it instead

cfgpins-ao.4c: N/C: no internal connection (Pin Functions p4); MIC5205's BYP pin sits here, so the 470 pF BYP cap of a MIC5205 layout is simply not fitted

specs-o.en_note-s: internal 500 k smart enable pulldown (disconnected once VEN > VEN(HI)); EN floating = off

en_source-o.table-s: 5.5 Electrical Characteristics: VEN(LOW) 0.3 V, VEN(HI) 0.9 V (VIN 1.6-6.0 V); REN(PULL-DOWN) 500 kOhm

specs-o.dropout_note-s: 145 mV max at 300 mA, 2.5 V <= VOUT < 5.5 V, DBV package (p6)
specs-o.rth_source-s: 5.4 Thermal Information p6, DBV (SOT-23) RthetaJA 187.1 C/W (JEDEC board)

ilimit_source-o.table-s: 5.5 Electrical Characteristics: ICL 360 / 520 / 730 mA (DQN; DBV row given for VOUT < 1.5 V with the same limits); ISC 160 mA at VOUT = 0 V

cout_source-o.table-s: 5.3 Recommended Operating Conditions: COUT 1 uF min / 200 uF max, ESR 100 mOhm max; note 3: effective output capacitance 0.47 uF min and 200 uF max required for stability

iout_source-o.table-s: 5.3 Recommended Operating Conditions: VIN 1.6-6.0 V, IOUT 0-300 mA

specs-o.replaces_s: MIC5205-2.8YM5-TR: same SOT-23-5 IN/GND/EN/OUT on pins 1/2/3/5; pin 4 is N/C here (MIC5205 BYP), so a MIC5205 footprint takes it with the BYP cap left off. Unlike MIC5205, it publishes load-transient figures

load_regulation_source-o.table-s: 5.5 Electrical Characteristics: Load regulation IOUT = 1 mA to 300 mA (DBV package) 19 mV
load_regulation_source-o.derived: 19 mV / 0.299 A = 63.5 mV/A over the full range; the 1-50 mA end is steeper than the linear part (Figure 5-7)

load_regulation-ao.fig-s: Figure 5-7. Load Regulation vs IOUT (DBV package)
load_regulation-ao.derived-s: TJ = 25 C trace read at 300 dpi: -8.5 mV at 50 mA, -20.0 mV at 300 mA -> 11.5 mV / 0.25 A = 46 mV/A. Caption says VIN = 2.8 V; the page header gives VIN = VOUT(NOM) + 0.3 V = 3.1 V, which is what an LDO out of dropout needs

load_transient-ao.conditions_source-s: Typical Characteristics header p16: VIN = VOUT(NOM) + 0.3 V, VOUT = 2.8 V, CIN = 1 uF, COUT = 1 uF, TA = 25 C
load_transient-ao.read-s: vector plot, pdf-graph points mapped to the right axis (AC-coupled mV) and checked on a render: +2 mV before the step, -48 mV at the trough; 300 -> 1 mA: -10.6 mV before, +6.6 mV peak
pdf-graph points mapped to the right axis: +2.6 mV before, -88.9 mV trough; 300 -> 1 mA: -10.5 mV before, +21.3 mV peak
from a true 0 mA start: +3.7 mV before, -188.8 mV trough; 300 -> 0 mA: -20 mV before, about -0.5 mV peak
+2.8 mV before, -188.2 mV trough; 300 -> 0 mA: -20 mV before, +11 mV peak

specs-o.load_transient_note-s: All four rising steps at COUT = 1 uF (the minimum); a 0 mA start dips about 4x deeper than 1 mA. Figures are drawn at VIN 3.1 V, not 5 V. An LDO's response is set by its loop and COUT rather than by VIN headroom, but that is not a datasheet curve

not_stated-o.output_impedance_mohm: no Zout curve (Typical Characteristics p8-22: line/load regulation, accuracy, dropout, IGND, current limit, load/line transient, PSRR, noise, start-up)
not_stated-o.efficiency_pct: not plotted (LDO): input current = output current + IGND (2000 uA max at 300 mA, p6)

source-o.figure-s: Figure 7-4. TPS7A20 Typical Application (1.0 uF in and out, EN to IN)
